due_when.clears_when: the docker-logs grep is changed from free-text keyword matching (which can capture a raw value on the same line) to a fixed enumerated set of known-safe IBC status phrases, or captured lines are pattern-scrubbed/redacted before being posted to the public issue comment or step summary

origin.rerun: grep -n "grep -iE" .github/workflows/vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test.yml; review the most recent run's posted issue comment / step summary (if any exist) for a captured line that contains a raw credential value rather than a status phrase

what: vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test.yml's remote log-tail step (.github/workflows/vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test.yml:199-201) greps the throwaway live-IBKR container's docker logs for a keyword set that includes the literal word 'password' (alongside 'incorrect', 'denied', 'rejected', etc.), and the matching lines are posted VERBATIM (last 6000 chars via `out.slice(-6000)`, line 232) into a public GitHub issue comment, or into the run's public $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY on workflow_dispatch (line 240) -- this repository is public. Credential material itself is handled correctly everywhere else in the file (staged to a file, scp'd, shredded, passed via --env-file, never in argv/log per the file's own header claim, verified). But if the ib-gateway/IBC container image ever emits a raw credential value on a login-failure/debug log line -- a documented behavior class for TWS/IBC verbose logs -- that value would be captured by this grep and published. NOT CONFIRMED to have occurred: no live login was triggered to test this (doing so would itself be an inappropriate live-credential test), so this is a plausible, unverified risk from code inspection, not an observed leak.
